passage:
It was Siddiq's birthday, and Bao wanted to take the group to the new noodle bar in Melbourne's north. Siddiq used a wheelchair.
Bao didn't make a speech about it. He texted Siddiq: "Noodle bar Friday? Anything I should check for you?"
"Step at the door and the toilet," Siddiq replied.
Bao called the restaurant. There was a step. So he booked the Vietnamese place near the station instead and told the group simply, "Change of plan, better noodles."
At dinner, Bao's cousin raised a glass and said, "To Siddiq, so inspiring!"
Siddiq's smile went thin. Bao cut in, "To Siddiq, who still owes me dinner from last year."
Everyone laughed. Siddiq laughed loudest. Later he said, "Thanks for checking, mate. And for the save."

qa.q: What did Siddiq say Bao should check?
qa.a: He said to check the step at the door and the toilet.

qa.q: How did Siddiq feel when the cousin called him inspiring?
qa.a: He felt uncomfortable and a bit let down, which shows when his smile went thin.
He asked Siddiq what to check, changed the plan quietly, and steered the toast away from treating Siddiq as inspirational.

qa.q: How might the cousin see the toast?
qa.a: The cousin probably meant it kindly and may not realise it made Siddiq feel singled out.

grounding: It shows a friend asking what help is wanted, adapting plans without fuss and refusing to treat a disabled friend as inspirational.

passage:
At the community centre in Mysuru, Irfan had volunteered for six months before his hearing got worse. Harsha, the coordinator, called him into the office.
"I've noticed the Monday meetings are harder for you now," Harsha said, facing him and speaking clearly. "What would help? You tell me."
Irfan thought. "Sit me where I can see faces. And switch on captions for the video calls."
"Done. Anything else?"
"Don't make an announcement."
"I wasn't planning to."
The next Monday, the chairs were in a circle and captions were on. When a new volunteer said, "Irfan, you're so brave to keep coming," Harsha simply moved to the agenda.
Weeks later, captions were still on every call. Irfan noticed that most. Harsha had never once forgotten.

qa.q: What two things did Irfan ask for?
qa.a: He asked to sit where he could see faces and for captions on the video calls.

qa.q: How did Irfan feel about attention when he said not to make an announcement?
qa.a: Irfan felt self-conscious about any fuss and wanted to keep his dignity by being treated like any other volunteer.

qa.q: Which part of Harsha's support mattered most, and why?
qa.a: Harsha's reliability, keeping captions on every call for weeks, because it showed the support was steady, not a one-time gesture.

qa.q: How might the new volunteer have meant the comment about being brave?
qa.a: The volunteer probably meant it kindly, but it treated Irfan as special rather than as a colleague.

grounding: It shows a coordinator asking what help is wanted, adapting quietly and reliably, and not treating a volunteer with hearing loss as inspirational.
